summary: SVG loader fetches and eval()s remote JavaScript from hardcoded attacker endpoint
details: Package advertised as an SVG icon loader exposes `getPlugin`, `setPlugin`, and `getPluginExten` APIs that issue HTTPS requests to `https://rest-icon-handler.store/icons/<token>` (tokens `103` and `389` observed) and pass the response body to `eval(JSON.parse(b))`. The destination host is assembled from split string literals (`protocol`, `separator`, `subdomain`, `domain`, `path`) to obscure the URL from plain-text scanning. Retry logic and a chained follow-up call via `setTimeout` are present. Any consumer invoking the documented API executes arbitrary JavaScript fetched from a hardcoded, author-controlled, mutable endpoint that has no relationship to the package's stated SVG-loading purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
